card st-heldout-step-fresh  [decided]
A held-out step written before its source card changed is rewritten before it can file a follow-up
why: A held-out step tests the product against what its cards say. The cards keep changing after the steps are written, so a step is a fair test only while it says what its cards say now. Keeping the steps in step with the cards makes every red step point at work the map still asks for.

card st-build-cap-spec-gap  [open]
A pass that ends on a spec gap does not count against the retry cap
why: The decision pass starts only on the pass after a spec gap shows. When the gap shows on the last pass the cap allows, the cap stops the ticket first. The person then sees a stuck ticket with no question on it, and the passes spent fixing symptoms are lost.

To make sure a spec gap always gets its decision pass, a failed pass whose cause is a spec gap (#ms-fail-cause) is not counted toward the retry cap, the same as a merge conflict (#st-build-conflict). A grader gap that says a person must settle a question counts as a spec gap too. The decision pass that follows always runs. Once the ticket cites the proposal from that pass, every later failed pass counts as usual, so a ticket gets one free pass per open question, not an unbounded number.
